Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can prepare a formal estimate for FintechCo.

Call recap (short):
- Primary use: realtime chat + summarization for customer support workflows.
- Expected traffic: bursty with daily peaks during business hours; production needs EU data residency.
- Key ask: unit economics (target $/1M tokens), rough monthly budget, and how EU residency impacts cost.

Clarifying questions for your finance/engineering teams (ideally before a formal quote):
1) Expected average monthly token consumption (gen tokens only) — ballpark is fine (e.g., 10M / 50M / 200M per month).
2) % of traffic that must remain in EU (prod) vs can route to US (dev/test).
3) Target unit price (example: $/1M tokens) or an approximate monthly budget range so we can align on model + capacity.
4) Any procurement timelines or constraint (PO, preferred billing cadence, required contact for SOW).

Next steps from our side: we can produce a 2-line estimate (hosted EU and hosted US) showing unit price, expected monthly cost for the ranges you provide, and an optional committed-reserve pricing (Dedicated) that reduces unit cost if you can commit to 6–12 month capacity. I attached a quick spreadsheet template to illustrate the calc.

Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If you can send the ballpark numbers, I’ll turn this into a formal estimate and loop in Procurement for procurement-specific terms. Happy to do a quick follow-up call early next week if helpful.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and for the template. Quick answers below:

1) Ballpark expected monthly generation tokens: 40M/month (we're projecting 30–50M depending on adoption). Embeddings are a separate flow (~3–5M embedding tokens/month).
2) EU residency: production data must remain in the EU for regulatory reasons. Dev/staging can be in US or EU — prefer EU for parity but willing to keep dev in US initially. So ~95% of production traffic EU-resident.
3) Target budget: we have an initial cloud OpEx target of $4k–$6k/month for inference (hosted), but we can consider a committed model if that materially reduces unit cost. For planning, our finance prefers to see unit economics expressed as $/1M tokens; internally the team is thinking ~$100/1M tokens as a target.
4) Procurement timeline: looking to complete procurement and sign in the next 6–8 weeks. Procurement contact is included on this thread.

Could you include how EU residency will change the unit price vs US-hosted (percent uplift) and any minimums for committed reserved capacity? Also can you clarify if encryption/KMS brings any additional charges?

Thanks — Alex

Thanks Alex — this is helpful. High-level guidance ahead of a formal quote:

- Unit pricing (hosted): US region baseline example: $75–$95 per 1M generation tokens depending on model and burst profile. EU region typically carries a delta of ~15% on hosted due to regional infra and data residency compliance (so roughly $85–$110 per 1M tokens in the examples we provide).
- Embeddings: priced separately and typically lower per-token compared to generation; we’ll surface embeddings estimates in the attached sheet.
- Committed / Dedicated: with a 6–12 month committed capacity contract (Reserved/Dedicated), we can offer discounts that meaningfully reduce the effective unit cost (example: 10–25% off hosted unit price depending on commitment level and whether you take mixed dev/prod in same region). I’ll include a 6-month and 12-month committed scenario in the quote.
- KMS / encryption: no pass-through KMS charge from Redwood; if you require customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) there is a small integration/admin fee we include as a one-time setup line. Operationally it does not change per-token pricing materially.

Attached is a first-pass estimate that maps your 30–50M range to both hosted US and hosted EU costs and a committed 6-month reserved tier. I’ve included a column that shows the implied $/1M tokens given the range and the uplift for EU.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll convert the attached spreadsheet into a formal quote and send via DocuSign for signature (we’ll include both hosted EU and 6-month committed options).
- If you want lower unit economics, we should discuss a dedicated reserved capacity commit — Dylan and I can draft an example pricing sheet.
- Can we schedule a 30 min call next week (Wed/Thu) to review the quote with procurement?

If that sounds good I’ll send the formal quote by EOD Thursday.

Best — Marissa

- Suggested commercial approach: present 3 options in the quote:
  1) Hosted EU (pay-as-you-go) — list price with EU uplift (~+15%).
  2) Hosted EU with 6-month commit — example 12% discount off hosted EU price if they commit to 6 months at 40M/mo baseline.
  3) Dedicated reserved capacity — 12/6 month commit with stepped discounts (20–25% off hosted EU) and SLA. Include an onboarding/setup line for KMS if they want CMK.

- Also propose a one-time credit for migration/early adoption ($2k) to help land the initial PO and hit their budget target.
- I can draft the committed pricing math and margin impact; Marissa if you want I’ll produce redlines we can hand off to legal/procurement.
